extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary XML/PDF locators; mechanism claims are bounded to model-membrane biophysical evidence and do not assert a fully resolved cellular killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: β-SB056-lin has stronger antimicrobial activity than SB056-lin and the paper links this to enhanced amphipathic β-strand formation in lipid bilayers.
direct_assay_types: MIC table interpreted with membrane-binding CD/SRCD/NMR assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism evidence is from lipid model systems and biophysical readouts; it is not a direct bacterial membrane permeabilization assay in live cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Tryptophan fluorescence, CD/SRCD, and solid-state NMR support membrane binding, β-stranded folding/aggregation, and stronger lipid bilayer perturbation for the optimized peptide under anionic lipid conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SB056-lin and β-SB056-lin in POPC/POPG lipid model systems
mechanism_claims.limitations: No exact curve-derived binding constants were curated because local material supplies plotted curves/captions rather than a structured numeric table.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The optimized β-SB056-lin shows higher hemolysis than SB056-lin at the upper tested concentrations, consistent with stronger interaction with zwitterionic mammalian-cell model surfaces.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: human erythrocyte toxicity context for β-SB056-lin versus SB056-lin
mechanism_claims.limitations: Hemolysis is a toxicity/safety context, not the antimicrobial mechanism endpoint.

caution_findings.rationale: Mechanism wording is bounded to direct biophysical model-membrane evidence.
